title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第十二 江謐 荀伯玉
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 12: Jiang Mi, Xun Boyu
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第十二 江謐 荀伯玉 Volume 31 Biographies 12: Jiang Mi, Xun Boyu

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷三十一‧列傳第十二

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 31 — Biography 12
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 31 — Biography 12

sentences.zh: 江謐 荀伯玉

translations.literal: Jiang Mi; Xun Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mi; Xun Boyu

sentences.zh: 江謐字令和，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Mi styled Linghe was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mi, styled Linghe, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖秉之，臨海太守，宋世清吏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bingzhi was administrator of Linhai, an upright officer of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bingzhi had been administrator of Linhai, a scrupulous officer under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父徽，尚書都官郎，吳令，爲太初所殺。

translations.literal: His father Hui was an aide in the Ministry of Works' punishment bureau and magistrate of Wu, and was killed in the Taichu turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served as an aide in the ministry of works' punishment bureau and as magistrate of Wu, and was slain in the Taichu reign.

sentences.zh: 謐繫尚方，孝武平京邑，乃得出。

translations.literal: Mi was held in the imperial workshops; when Emperor Xiaowu pacified the capital region he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was detained in the imperial workshops; when Emperor Xiaowu pacified the capital he was let out.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請，輔國行參軍，于湖令，強濟稱職。

translations.literal: Leaving lacquer he became attendant at court, acting aide to the general who supports the state, and magistrate of Yuhu—resolute and able, he was praised as fit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving lacquer he became attendant at court, acting aide to the general who supports the state, and magistrate of Yuhu—bold and capable, he was held to have done the office justice.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝爲南豫州，謐傾身奉之，爲帝所親待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song held Southern Yuzhou, Mi devoted himself wholly to the prince and was treated with close favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Song was posted at Southern Yu, Mi threw himself into the prince's service and won intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 卽位，以爲驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: Upon his accession, Mi was made aide to the general who spreads might.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Mi was named aide to the general who spreads might.

sentences.zh: 弟蒙貌醜，帝常召見狎侮之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Meng was ugly of face; the emperor would often summon him for familiar mockery.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Meng had an ugly face; the emperor would often call him in to tease him familiarly.

sentences.zh: 謐轉尚書度支郎，俄遷右丞，兼比部郎。

translations.literal: Mi was moved to revenue bureau aide in the ministry, soon promoted to right vice director, with added duty as comparison-bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was transferred to revenue aide in the ministry, then soon made right vice director, with added duty in the comparison bureau.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，江夏王義恭第十五女卒，年十九，未笄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before her capping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before she had been capped.

sentences.zh: 禮官議從成人服，諸王服大功。

translations.literal: The ritual officers debated following the dress of a full adult; the princes were to wear dafu mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers argued for the dress of a full adult; the princes were to wear dafu mourning.

sentences.zh: 左丞孫敻重奏：「《禮記》女子十五而笄，鄭云應年許嫁者也。

translations.literal: Left vice director Sun Xuan memorialized again: 「In the Book of Rites a girl is capped at fifteen; Zheng Xuan says this is the year when she ought to be betrothed.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Sun Xuan memorialized again: 「The Book of Rites caps a girl at fifteen; Zheng Xuan says that is the year when she ought to be pledged in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其未許嫁者，則二十而笄。

translations.literal: If she has not been pledged, then she is capped at twenty.
translations.idiomatic: If she has not been pledged, she is capped at twenty.

sentences.zh: 射慈云十九猶爲殤。

translations.literal: She Ci says that at nineteen one is still in shang mourning.
translations.idiomatic: She Ci holds that at nineteen one is still in shang mourning.

sentences.zh: 禮官違越經典，於禮無據。

translations.literal: The ritual officers have overstepped the canon and have no footing in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers have overstepped the canon and have no footing in ritual.

sentences.zh: 」博士太常以下結免贖論；

translations.literal: 」The erudites and the grand steward down banded together for exemption by ransom;
translations.idiomatic: 」The erudites and the grand steward down banded together for exemption by ransom;

sentences.zh: 謐坐杖督五十，奪勞百日。

translations.literal: Mi was sentenced to fifty blows with the staff and stripped of merit credit for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was sentenced to fifty blows with the staff and stripped of merit credit for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 謐又奏：「敻先不研辨，混同謬議。

translations.literal: Mi memorialized again: 「Xuan earlier failed to examine and distinguish, and mingled his own with the mistaken opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Mi memorialized again: 「Xuan earlier failed to examine the matter and mingled his name with the mistaken opinion.

sentences.zh: 准以事例，亦宜及咎。

translations.literal: By precedent he too should share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent he too should share the blame.

sentences.zh: 」敻又結免贖論。

translations.literal: 」Xuan again banded together for exemption by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xuan again banded together for exemption by ransom.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 出爲建平王景素冠軍長史、長沙內史，行湘州事。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk under Prince of Jianping Jingsu's general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk to Prince of Jianping Jingsu under the general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang affairs.

sentences.zh: 政治苛刻。

translations.literal: His governance was harsh and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was harsh and exacting.

sentences.zh: 僧遵道人與謐情款，隨謐莅郡，犯小事，餓繫郡獄，僧遵裂三衣食之，旣盡而死。

translations.literal: The monk Seng Zun was on close terms with Mi and followed him to the commandery; for a small offense he was starved and held in the prefectural jail. Seng Zun tore his three layers of clothing to feed him; when they were gone he died.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Seng Zun was intimate with Mi and followed him to the prefecture; for a petty offense he was starved and held in the county jail. Seng Zun tore his three layers of clothing to feed him; when they were spent he died.

sentences.zh: 爲有司所奏，徵還。

translations.literal: The relevant offices impeached him and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices impeached him and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遇赦得免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he was spared by the general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, he was spared by the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 爲正員郎，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He became a regular-ranked attendant and general of the right army.
translations.idiomatic: He became a regular-ranked attendant and general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 太祖領南兖州，謐爲鎮軍長史、廣陵太守，入爲游擊將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder took Southern Yan, Mi was chief clerk of the army that guards the state and administrator of Guangling, then entered court as general of raiding attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Southern Yan, Mi was chief clerk of the army that guards the state and administrator of Guangling, then entered court as general of raiding attack.

sentences.zh: 性流俗，善趨勢利。

translations.literal: By nature he was commonplace and skilled at courting power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was commonplace and skilled at courting power and profit.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，朝野咸屬意建平王景素，謐深自委結，景素事敗，僅得免禍。

translations.literal: Late in the Yuanhui era court and countryside alike looked to Prince of Jianping Jingsu; Mi threw himself into a deep bond with him. When Jingsu's affair failed he barely escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanhui era court and countryside alike looked to Prince of Jianping Jingsu; Mi threw himself into a deep bond with him. When Jingsu's affair failed he barely escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王廢後，物情尚懷疑惑，謐獨竭誠歸事太祖，以本官領尚書左丞。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Cangwu was deposed, popular feeling still wavered in doubt; Mi alone gave himself wholly to the Founder and, in his present office, also led the ministry as left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Cangwu was deposed, popular feeling still hung in doubt; Mi alone gave himself wholly to the Founder and, in his present office, also led the ministry as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年，遷黃門侍郎，左丞如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming he was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate, left vice director unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming he was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate, left vice director unchanged.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，議加太祖黃鉞，謐所建也。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the grant of the golden battle-axe to the Founder was Mi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, the grant of the golden battle-axe to the Founder was Mi's proposal.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷吏部郎，稍被親待。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel and gradually won intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel and gradually won intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉諮議，領錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to adviser of the grand marshal and led the recording aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to adviser of the grand marshal and led the recording aide.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，爲右衞將軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he became general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established he became general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，遷侍中，出爲臨川王平西長史、冠軍將軍、長沙內史、行湘州留事，先遣之鎮，旣而驃騎豫章王嶷領湘州，以謐爲長史，將軍、內史、知州留事如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Liao took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Liao took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封永新縣伯，四百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Baron of Yongxin, four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Yongxin, four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三年，爲左民尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he became minister of the left populace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became minister of the left populace.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子出閤用文武主帥，皆以委謐。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial sons left the inner quarters and needed civil and military commanders, the choice fell to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial sons left the inner quarters and needed civil and military commanders, the choice fell to Mi.

sentences.zh: 尋敕曰：「江謐寒士，誠當不得競等華儕。

translations.literal: Soon an edict said: 「Jiang Mi is a man of humble birth and truly ought not to vie with the splendid peers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict said: 「Jiang Mi is a man of humble birth and truly ought not to vie with the splendid peers.

sentences.zh: 然甚有才幹，堪爲委遇，可遷掌吏部。」

translations.literal: Yet he is very able and fit to be entrusted; he may be moved to head the ministry of personnel.」
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is very able and fit to be entrusted; he may be moved to head the ministry of personnel.」

sentences.zh: 謐才長刀筆，所在事辦。

translations.literal: Mi's talent lay in clerical and legal work; wherever he was posted, affairs were handled.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's talent lay in clerical and legal work; wherever he was posted, affairs were handled.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，謐稱疾不入，衆頗疑其怨不豫顧命也。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, Mi claimed illness and did not attend; many suspected he resented not being named in the deathbed testament.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder died, Mi claimed illness and did not attend; many suspected he resented not being named in the deathbed testament.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，謐又不遷官，以此怨望。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Mi was again not promoted, and from this he bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Mi was again not promoted, and from this he bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 時世祖不豫，謐詣豫章王嶷請閒曰：「至尊非起疾，東宮又非才，公今欲作何計？

translations.literal: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and asked for a private word, saying: 「The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and asked for a private word, saying: 「The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?

sentences.zh: 」世祖知之，出謐爲征虜將軍、鎮北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: 」Shizu learned of it and sent Mi out as general who campaigns against barbarians, chief clerk of the army that guards the north, and administrator of Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shizu learned of it and sent Mi out as general who campaigns against barbarians, chief clerk of the army that guards the north, and administrator of Southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 未發，上使御史中丞沈沖奏謐前後罪曰：「謐少懷輕躁，長習諂薄，交無義合，行必利動。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the throne had the censor-in-chief Shen Chong impeach Mi's offenses past and present, saying: 「From youth Mi has harbored levity and rashness; grown, he has made a habit of flattery and shallowness. His associations lack righteous bond; his conduct always follows profit.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, the throne had the censor-in-chief Shen Chong impeach Mi's offenses past and present, saying: 「From youth Mi has harbored levity and rashness; grown, he has made a habit of flattery and shallowness. His associations lack righteous bond; his conduct always follows profit.

sentences.zh: 特以奕世更局，見擢宋朝，而阿諛內外，貨賂公行，咎盈憲簡，戾彰朝聽，輿金輦寶，取容近習。

translations.literal: Only because generations had changed dynasties was he advanced under the Song; yet he flattered inside and out, gifts and bribes ran openly, faults overflowed the legal records, offenses showed in court hearings, and he carted gold and lavished treasures to win favor from intimate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His line had merely ridden a change of dynasties into Song service, yet he flattered court and camp alike, bribes ran in the open, fault piled up in the statutes, outrage broke through at every hearing, and he hauled gold and jewels to buy favor from the emperor's intimates.

sentences.zh: 以沈攸之地勝兵強，終當得志，委心託身，歲暮相結。

translations.literal: Because Shen Youzhi's territory was strong in troops and would in the end prevail, he entrusted heart and body and bonded with him at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi held rich lands and a strong army, Mi judged that he would prevail in the end and threw in his lot, binding himself to him as the year closed.

sentences.zh: 以劉景素親屬望重，物應樂推，獻誠薦子，窺窬非望。

translations.literal: Because Liu Jingsu, as imperial kin, bore heavy expectation and the world ought to joyously raise him, he offered sincerity and recommended his son, peering at improper ambition.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jingsu, Prince Jingsu of Jianping, stood high in kinship and men were ready to lift him, Mi offered his loyalty, pushed forward his son, and eyed what was not his to take.

sentences.zh: 時艱網漏，得全首領。

translations.literal: Times were hard and the net had holes; he kept his head.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled days the law had gaps, and he alone kept his head.

sentences.zh: 太祖匡飭天地，方弘遠圖，薄其難洗之瑕，許其革音之效，加以非分之寵，推以不次之榮，列迹勳良，比肩朝德。

translations.literal: The founding emperor was rectifying heaven and earth and opening a far-reaching design; he overlooked stains hard to wash away, granted the effect of reforming his tone, added favor beyond measure, pushed unscheduled glory, ranked him among meritorious worthies, and set him shoulder to shoulder with court virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was setting heaven and earth in order and laying distant plans; he passed over stains that would not wash clean, credited Mi with a change of heart, heaped on him favor beyond his due, raised him to honors out of turn, and ranked him among the meritorious, shoulder to shoulder with the court's best.

sentences.zh: 以往者微勤，刀筆小用，賞廁河山，任忝出入。

translations.literal: For past slight diligence and petty clerkly use he was rewarded with enfeoffment in river and mountain, and office unworthy of moving in and out of court.
translations.idiomatic: For trifling past service and a knack with the brush he was enfeoffed among river and hill, and given posts he was unfit to hold at court.

sentences.zh: 輕險之性，在貴彌彰；

translations.literal: A nature of lightness and danger showed all the more once he was elevated;
translations.idiomatic: His reckless, treacherous temper grew only sharper once he rose;

sentences.zh: 貪昧之情，雖富無滿。

translations.literal: greedy obtuseness, though rich, was never satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: his greed, for all his wealth, was never filled.

sentences.zh: 重莅湘部，顯行斷盜；

translations.literal: Returning again to the Xiang command he openly practiced extortion and robbery;
translations.idiomatic: Posted again to Xiang, he openly plundered and stole;

sentences.zh: 及居銓衡，肆意受納。

translations.literal: when he took the personnel scales he accepted bribes at will.
translations.idiomatic: and once he held the ministry scales he took gifts as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 連席同乘，皆詖黷舊侶；

translations.literal: Those who shared mat and carriage were all sycophantic old companions;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever shared his mat or his carriage was an old crony grown bold in presumption;

sentences.zh: 密筵閑讌，必貨賄常客。

translations.literal: at secret feasts and leisurely banquets he always bribed his regular guests.
translations.idiomatic: at private feasts he always paid off the men who kept coming back.

sentences.zh: 理合升進者，以爲己惠；

translations.literal: Whoever by reason ought to be promoted he treated as a personal favor;
translations.idiomatic: Men who deserved promotion he treated as personal debts owed to him;

sentences.zh: 事宜貶退者，竝稱中旨。

translations.literal: whoever by affairs ought to be demoted he all declared to match the center's intent.
translations.idiomatic: men who ought to fall he dismissed as carrying out the throne's will.

sentences.zh: 謂販鬻威權，姦自不露，欺主罔上，謗議可掩。

translations.literal: He thought that selling power and authority, his wickedness would not show, that deceiving the lord and deceiving superiors, slander could be covered.
translations.idiomatic: He believed he could trade in power without exposure, deceive his sovereign and hoodwink his superiors, and smother every whisper against him.

sentences.zh: 先帝寢疾彌留，人神憂震。

translations.literal: The former emperor's illness lingered; men and spirits were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor lay long in his sickness, heaven and earth trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 謐託病私舍，曾無變容。

translations.literal: Mi feigned illness in a private residence and never once changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: Mi pleaded illness at home and never once altered his face.

sentences.zh: 國諱經旬，甫蹔入殿，參訪遺詔，覘忖時旨。

translations.literal: National mourning ran ten days before he briefly entered the hall, consulted on the surviving will, and peered at the timely intent.
translations.idiomatic: Not until mourning had run ten days did he slip into the hall, inquire after the testament, and probe what the moment would bear.

sentences.zh: 以身列朝流，宜蒙兼帶，先顧不逮，舊位無加，遂崇飾惡言，肆醜縱悖，譏誹朝政，訕毀皇猷，徧蚩忠賢，歷詆台相。

translations.literal: As one ranked in the court stream he ought to have received concurrent posts; early care did not reach him and his old rank was not raised, so he exalted wicked words, unleashed ugliness and rash rebellion, mocked court administration, defamed the imperial design, everywhere slandered loyal worthies, and repeatedly slandered ministry chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: As a man of standing in court he should have gained added offices; when favor passed him by and his old rank stood still, he dressed up malice, let loose every ugly excess, mocked the government, defamed the throne's design, slandered loyal men wherever he could, and tore down the ministers one after another.

sentences.zh: 至於蕃岳入授，列代恒規，勳戚出撫，前王彝則。

translations.literal: As for feudal princes entering to receive instruction, that was the constant rule of successive generations; merit kin going out to soothe was the former kings' permanent law.
translations.idiomatic: Princes entering court to receive their charge was the rule of age after age; kinsmen of merit going out to govern was the law the former kings had set.

sentences.zh: 而謐妄發樞機，坐構囂論。

translations.literal: Yet Mi rashly raised pivotal mechanisms and sat constructing clamorous debate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mi meddled with the hinges of power and sat stirring noisy quarrels.

sentences.zh: 復敢貶謗儲后，不顧辭端，毀折宗王，每窮舌杪。

translations.literal: Again he dared denigrate the heir apparent, heedless of rhetorical edge, ruined and bent imperial clan princes, and every time drove speech to the tip of the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: He dared again to run down the heir, reckless of how far his words went, and bent and broke the imperial princes until his tongue had no room left to twist.

sentences.zh: 皆云誥誓乖禮，崇樹失宜，仰指天，俯畫地，希幸災故，以申積憤。

translations.literal: All said imperial commands and oaths violated ritual, that elevation and planting were improper; pointing up at heaven and drawing on the earth below, he hoped for calamity and disaster to vent accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He cried that edicts and oaths broke ritual, that honors and appointments were wrong; he pointed at heaven, traced lines on the earth, and prayed for disaster to pour out the spite he had stored up.

sentences.zh: 犯上之迹旣彰，反噬之情已著。

translations.literal: Signs of offending superiors were already clear; the will to bite back was already plain.
translations.idiomatic: His defiance of superiors was plain to see; his urge to turn and bite was plain as well.

sentences.zh: 請免官削爵土，收送廷尉獄治罪。

translations.literal: We ask that he be dismissed from office, his fief lands stripped, seized and sent to the Minister of Justice prison for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that he be removed from office, stripped of his fief, seized, and sent to the Minister of Justice for trial.

sentences.zh: 」詔賜死，時年五十二。

translations.literal: 」An edict granted death by suicide; he was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict ordered him to take his own life. He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 子介，建武中，爲吳令，治亦深切。

translations.literal: His son Jie, in the Jianwu era, was magistrate of Wu; his governance was likewise severe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie, in the Jianwu reign, served as magistrate of Wu, and governed with the same harsh hand.

sentences.zh: 民閒榜死人髑髏爲謐首，介棄官而去。

translations.literal: Among the people someone posted a dead man's skull as Mi's head; Jie abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the streets someone nailed up a dead man's skull as Mi's head; Jie threw down his office and fled.

sentences.zh: 荀伯玉字弄璋，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Xun Boyu, styled Nongzhang, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Boyu, styled Nongzhang, came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 祖永，南譙太守，父闡之，給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong was Administrator of Southern Qiao; his father Chanzhi was Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong had been administrator of Southern Qiao; his father Chanzhi, attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 伯玉少爲柳元景撫軍板行參軍，南徐州祭酒，晉安王子勛鎮軍行參軍。

translations.literal: In youth Boyu was acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's Pacifier Army staff, libationer of South Xuzhou, and acting adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's Stabilizing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Young, Boyu served as acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's pacifier-army staff, as libationer of southern Xuzhou, and as acting adjutant on the stabilizing army of Prince Zixun of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，子勛舉事，伯玉友人孫沖爲將帥，伯玉隷其驅使，封新亭侯。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taishi, Zixun raised arms; Boyu's friend Sun Chong became a commander, and Boyu followed his orders and was enfeoffed Marquis of Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened, Zixun rose in rebellion; Boyu's friend Sun Chong took command, and Boyu rode under him and was enfeoffed Marquis of Xinting.

sentences.zh: 事敗，伯玉還都賣卜自業。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, Boyu returned to the capital and sold divination for a living.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, Boyu went back to the capital and made his living casting lots.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素聞而招之，伯玉不往。

translations.literal: Prince Jingsu of Jianping heard and recruited him; Boyu did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingsu of Jianping heard of him and called him in; Boyu would not go.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，伯玉歸身結事，爲太祖冠軍刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor held Huaiyin, Boyu pledged himself and served him, and was made the founding emperor's Champion Army adjutant for prisons and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: While the founding emperor was posted at Huaiyin, Boyu threw himself on his service and became adjutant for prisons under the champion army.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲明帝所疑，及徵爲黃門郎，深懷憂慮。

translations.literal: The founding emperor was suspected by Emperor Ming; when he was summoned as Yellow Gate Gentleman he was deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor fell under Emperor Ming's suspicion; when the summons came to make him a yellow gate gentleman, his heart was full of dread.

sentences.zh: 伯玉勸太祖遣數十騎入虜界，安置標榜，於是虜游騎數百履行界上，太祖以聞，猶懼不得留，令伯玉卜，伯玉斷卦不成行，而明帝詔果復太祖本任，由是見親待。

translations.literal: Boyu urged the founding emperor to send several dozen horsemen into the enemy frontier to set up markers; thereupon several hundred enemy patrol horsemen rode the border. The founding emperor reported it, yet still feared he could not remain; he had Boyu divine, and Boyu read the hexagram as unfit to travel; Emperor Ming's edict indeed restored the founding emperor to his former post, and from this he was treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu urged him to send a few dozen riders into the northern marches and set up boundary markers; soon hundreds of enemy patrols were riding the line. The founding emperor reported it, yet still feared the court would recall him and had Boyu cast the hexagrams; Boyu read that the journey would not succeed, and Emperor Ming's edict in fact restored him to his old command. From that day he was held close.

sentences.zh: 從太祖還都，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: Following the founding emperor back to the capital, he was appointed Palace Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor returned to the capital, Boyu was made a palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 令伯玉看宅，知家事。

translations.literal: The founding emperor had Boyu watch the residence and manage household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor set him to watch the mansion and run the household.

sentences.zh: 世祖罷廣興還，立別宅，遣人於大宅掘樹數株，伯玉不與，馳以聞。

translations.literal: When Shizu ended Guangxing and returned, he established a separate residence and sent men to dig up several trees from the great mansion; Boyu would not allow it and hurried to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu left Guangxing and came back he built a separate house and sent men to dig up several trees from the main estate; Boyu refused and rode at once to report it.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「卿執之是也。

translations.literal: The founding emperor said: 「Your holding firm is right.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said, 「You were right to stand firm.

sentences.zh: 」轉太祖平南府，晉熙王府參軍。

translations.literal: 」He was shifted to the founding emperor's Pacify-the-South headquarters and staff officer of the Prince of Jinxi's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was moved to the pacify-the-south headquarters and made staff officer in the Prince of Jinxi's household.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲南兖州，伯玉轉爲上鎮軍中兵參軍，帶廣陵令。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor held southern Yanzhou, Boyu became adjutant of the upper camp army and concurrently magistrate of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took southern Yanzhou, Boyu became adjutant of the upper camp and served concurrently as magistrate of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 除羽林監，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Feathered Forest and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named director of the feathered forest and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖在淮南，伯玉假還廣陵，夢上廣陵城南樓上，有二青衣小兒語伯玉云：「草中肅，九五相追逐。

translations.literal: At first, while the founding emperor was in Huainan, Boyu took leave to Guangling and dreamed that he was on the south tower of Guangling city; two boys in blue said to Boyu: 「Su in the grass; nine-fives pursue each other.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while the founding emperor was in Huainan, Boyu went home on leave to Guangling and dreamed he stood on the city's south tower; two boys in blue called to him, 「Amid the grass, su—nine-fives in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」伯玉視城下人頭上皆有草。

translations.literal: 」Boyu looked below the city and saw grass on every man's head.
translations.idiomatic: 」He looked down and saw every man in the streets with grass on his head.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，伯玉又夢太祖乘船在廣陵北渚，見上兩掖下有翅不舒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi Boyu again dreamed that the founding emperor was in a boat at the north ford of Guangling and that under both armpits were wings not yet spread.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year seven he dreamed again that the founding emperor sailed a boat at Guangling's north ford, wings folded under both arms.

sentences.zh: 伯玉問何當舒，上曰：「却後三年。

translations.literal: Boyu asked when they would spread; the emperor said: 「Three years from now.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu asked when they would open; the emperor said, 「Three years hence.

sentences.zh: 」伯玉夢中自謂是呪師，向上唾呪之，凡六呪，有六龍出，兩掖下翅皆舒，還而復斂。

translations.literal: 」In the dream Boyu took himself for a curse-master, spat curses upward six times, six dragons emerged, the wings under both armpits spread and then closed again.
translations.idiomatic: 」In the dream Boyu thought himself a curse-master, spat six curses upward, six dragons rose, the wings under both arms opened, then folded shut again.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，而太祖破桂陽，威名大震。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui the founding emperor crushed Guiyang and his renown shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year two the founding emperor broke Guiyang, and his name thundered across the realm.

sentences.zh: 五年而廢蒼梧。

translations.literal: After five years the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Five years on, the throne cast down the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂伯玉曰：「卿時乘之夢，今且效矣。」

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said to Boyu: 「The dream you once had of riding—now it is coming true.」
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor told Boyu: 「That dream of yours about riding—see how it is being fulfilled.」

sentences.zh: 昇明初，仍爲太祖驃騎中兵參軍，除步兵校尉，不拜。

translations.literal: At the opening of Shengming he again served the Grand Ancestor as central-troop aide in the Marshal's headquarters; he was named Colonel of the Footsoldiers but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengming opened he again held central-troop aide in the Grand Ancestor's marshal staff; Colonel of the Footsoldiers was offered, and he declined.

sentences.zh: 仍帶濟陽太守，中兵如故。

translations.literal: He still held concurrent office as administrator of Jiyang; his central-troop post stood unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He still carried Jiyang as concurrent prefect; his central-troop duty was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 霸業旣建，伯玉忠勤盡心，常衞左右。

translations.literal: Once the founding enterprise was secure, Boyu served with loyal, tireless devotion and constantly guarded the Grand Ancestor's person.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding cause was won, Boyu gave himself over in loyal, tireless service and never left the Grand Ancestor's side.

sentences.zh: 加前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Front Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Front Army General.

sentences.zh: 隨太祖太尉府轉中兵，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor moved to the Grand Commandant's mansion, Boyu was shifted to central troops; his general's rank and prefecture stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: With the Grand Ancestor's transfer to the Grand Commandant's office, Boyu moved to the central troops; his general's title and prefecture stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封南豐縣子，四百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nanfeng, with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan's first year he was enfeoffed Viscount of Nanfeng, with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍，武陵王征虜司馬，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State and army aide on the Prince of Wuling's Pacify-the-Barbarians staff; his prefecture was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Assists the State and army aide to the Prince of Wuling on the Pacify-the-Barbarians staff, still holding his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙爲安成王冠軍司馬，轉豫章王司空諮議，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to champion army aide for the Prince of Ancheng, then to staff adviser under the Prince of Yuzhang as Minister of Works; his prefecture stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to champion aide for the Prince of Ancheng, then to staff adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang as Minister of Works, with his prefecture unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖在東宮，專斷用事，頗不如法。

translations.literal: While Shizu held the Eastern Palace he acted on his own authority and largely outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu was crown prince he ruled the Eastern Palace by fiat, and much of what he did sat outside the law.

sentences.zh: 任左右張景真，使領東宮主衣食官穀帛，賞賜什物，皆御所服用。

translations.literal: He entrusted his favorite Zhang Jingzhen and had him oversee the Eastern Palace offices for food, clothing, grain, and cloth; rewards and goods were all of the sort the inner palace used.
translations.idiomatic: He put his favorite Zhang Jingzhen in charge of the Eastern Palace commissaries for food, clothing, grain, and cloth; every gift and good was of the kind reserved for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 景真於南澗寺捨身齋，有元徽紫皮袴褶，餘物稱是。

translations.literal: At Nanjian Temple Jingzhen held a body-offering fast; he wore Yuanhui-era purple leather trousers and jacket, and his other things matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen took a body-offering fast at Nanjian Temple in Yuanhui purple leather coat and trousers, with the rest of his gear to match.

sentences.zh: 於樂遊設會，伎人皆著御衣。

translations.literal: At Leyou he gave a feast, and the performers all wore imperial dress.
translations.idiomatic: He held a feast at Leyou, and every performer wore robes from the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 又度絲錦與崑崙舶營貨，輙使傳令防送過南州津。

translations.literal: He also sent silk brocade out to Kunlun ships for trade, and whenever he did so he had runners posted to escort the goods past the Southern Province ferry.
translations.idiomatic: He also shipped silk brocade to Kunlun merchant vessels for trade, and each time had runners posted to see the cargo through the Southern Province crossing.

sentences.zh: 世祖拜陵還，景真白服乘畫舴艋，坐胡牀，觀者咸疑是太子。

translations.literal: When Shizu returned from paying respects at the tombs, Jingzhen wore white dress, rode a painted skiff, and sat on a folding camp-chair; onlookers all took him for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizu's return from the tombs, Jingzhen went in white, rode a painted skiff, and lolled on a camp-chair; the crowd mistook him for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 內外祗畏，莫敢有言。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the palace all stood in awe, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Court and capital alike stood in awe, and no one dared raise a word.

sentences.zh: 伯玉謂親人曰：「太子所爲，官終不知，豈得顧死蔽官耳目。

translations.literal: Boyu told his kin: 「What the crown prince is doing, the throne will never know of in the end—how can one choose death to cover the throne's eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: Boyu told his family: 「The crown prince is doing what the throne will never hear of in the end—who dies to blind the court to it?

sentences.zh: 我不啓聞，誰應啓者？

translations.literal: If I do not report it, who should?」
translations.idiomatic: If I do not speak, who will?」

sentences.zh: 」因世祖拜陵後密啓之。

translations.literal: Accordingly, after Shizu returned from the tombs he secretly memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: So after Shizu came back from the tombs he sent a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，檢校東宮。

translations.literal: The throne was furious and inspected the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The throne flew into a rage and sent men to search the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖還至方山，日暮將泊。

translations.literal: Shizu returned as far as Mount Fang; at dusk he was about to moor.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu came back as far as Mount Fang and at dusk meant to put in.

sentences.zh: 豫章王於東府乘飛東迎，具白上怒之意。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, from the Eastern Mansion, rode Flying East to meet him and fully explained the throne's anger.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang came out from the Eastern Mansion on Flying East to meet him and told him plainly how furious the throne was.

sentences.zh: 世祖夜歸，上亦停門籥待之，二更盡，方入宮。

translations.literal: Shizu returned that night; the throne too held the gate-bars open waiting for him, and only after the second watch had ended did he enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu came in by night; the throne kept the gates barred open for him, and not until the second watch was spent did he enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 上明日遣文惠太子、聞喜公子良宣敕，以景真罪狀示世祖。

translations.literal: The next day the throne sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Wenxi to proclaim the edict and show Shizu Jingzhen's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the throne sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Wenxi to read the edict and lay Jingzhen's crimes before Shizu.

sentences.zh: 稱太子令，收景真殺之。

translations.literal: In the crown prince's name Jingzhen was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the crown prince's name they took Jingzhen in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 世祖憂懼，稱疾月餘日。

translations.literal: Shizu was anxious and afraid, and pleaded illness for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu lived in fear and pleaded illness for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 上怒不解。

translations.literal: The throne's anger did not lift.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's wrath would not break.

sentences.zh: 晝卧太陽殿，王敬則直入，叩頭啓上曰：「官有天下日淺，太子無事被責，人情恐懼，願官往東宮解釋之。

translations.literal: At midday he lay down in the Hall of the Great Sun; Wang Jingze entered straight in, knocked his head to the floor, and reported: 「Your Majesty has held the realm only a short while; the crown prince has been blamed without cause, and men's hearts are afraid—may Your Majesty go to the Eastern Palace and set things right.
translations.idiomatic: At noon he lay down in the Hall of the Great Sun. Wang Jingze walked straight in, kowtowed, and said: 「Your Majesty has had the realm only a little while; the crown prince was punished without cause, and hearts are afraid—go to the Eastern Palace and make peace.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃幸宮，召諸王以下於玄圃園爲家宴，致醉乃還。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Ancestor then visited the palace, summoned all the princes down to a family feast in the Mystic Garden, and only when all were drunk did he return.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Grand Ancestor then went to the palace, called every prince down to a family feast in the Mystic Garden, and left only when all were drunk.

sentences.zh: 上嘉伯玉盡心，愈見親信，軍國密事，多委使之。

translations.literal: The throne praised Boyu's wholehearted service and trusted him all the more; military and state secrets were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne prized Boyu's wholehearted service and drew him closer still; military and state secrets went largely through his hands.

sentences.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「十敕五令，不如荀伯玉命。

translations.literal: Men of the time made a saying of it: 「Ten imperial edicts and five orders are not as good as one command from Xun Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran: 「Ten throne edicts and five orders weigh less than one word from Xun Boyu.

sentences.zh: 」世祖深怨伯玉。

translations.literal: 」Shizu deeply resented Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shizu hated Boyu to the bone.

sentences.zh: 上臨崩，指伯玉謂世祖曰：「此人事我忠，我身後，人必爲其作口過，汝勿信也。

translations.literal: As the throne lay dying he pointed at Boyu and told Shizu: 「This man served me with loyalty; after I am gone people will surely speak ill of him—do not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the throne pointed at Boyu and told Shizu: 「This man was loyal to me; after I am gone men will surely slander him—do not heed them.

sentences.zh: 可令往東宮長侍白澤，小却以南兖州處之。」

translations.literal: You may have him go to the Eastern Palace as chief attendant to Baize; later, with a slight demotion, place him in southern Yanzhou.」
translations.idiomatic: Send him to the Eastern Palace as chief attendant to Baize; later, with a small step down, give him southern Yanzhou.」

sentences.zh: 伯玉遭父憂，除冠軍將軍、南濮陽太守，未拜，除黃門郎，本官如故。

translations.literal: When Boyu entered mourning for his father he was named Champion General and administrator of southern Puyang; before he could accept he was named Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, his former offices standing as before.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father Boyu was named Champion General and southern Puyang; before he took up the post he was named Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖轉爲豫章王太尉諮議，太守如故。

translations.literal: Shizu, now Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant, made him staff adviser; his prefecture stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, as Prince of Yuzhang and Grand Commandant, named him staff adviser; his prefecture was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 俄遷散騎常侍，太守如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Regular Attendant; his prefecture stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was shifted to Regular Attendant, still holding his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯玉憂懼無計，上聞之，以其與垣崇祖善，慮相扇爲亂，加意撫之，伯玉乃安。

translations.literal: Boyu was anxious and at his wits' end; when the throne heard of it, because he was close to Yuan Chongzu he feared they would stir each other to revolt and treated him with added care—only then did Boyu settle.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was trapped in fear. The throne heard of it; knowing his tie to Yuan Chongzu, he feared the two would rouse each other to revolt and soothed him with special care—only then did Boyu grow calm.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，垣崇祖誅，伯玉并伏法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, Yuan Chongzu was executed, and Boyu was put to death with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's first year Yuan Chongzu was killed, and Boyu died by the same sentence.

sentences.zh: 初，善相墓者見伯玉家墓，謂其父曰：「當出暴貴而不久也。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man skilled at reading tombs saw the Boyu family grave and told his father: 「This line will produce sudden, towering rank—but not for long.」
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a tomb-reader saw the Boyu family burial and told his father: 「This house will rise to sudden glory—and not keep it long.」

sentences.zh: 」伯玉後聞之，曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。

translations.literal: 」When Boyu later heard of it he said: 「If one has heard the Way at dawn, one may die at dusk.」
translations.idiomatic: 」When Boyu heard it later he said: 「Hear the Way at dawn, and dusk is time enough to die.」

sentences.zh: 」死時年五十。

translations.literal: At his death he was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty at his death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：君老不事太子，義烈之遺訓也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: An elder who will not serve the crown prince—this is the fierce teaching left by men of principle.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The elder who will not serve the crown prince—that is the fierce lesson the principled leave behind.

sentences.zh: 欲夫專心所奉，在節無貳，雖人子之親，尚宜自別，則偏黨爲論，豈或傍啓。

translations.literal: To fix the heart on the one you serve, with loyalty that knows no second allegiance—even toward a son's own kin one should still stand apart; how then could faction be the argument, or a side report be offered?
translations.idiomatic: Fix the heart on the lord you serve, with loyalty that brooks no second master—even a son's bond should be set apart; how then make faction the plea, or whisper through another's door?

sentences.zh: 察江、荀之行也，雖異術而同亡。

translations.literal: When one weighs Jiang's conduct and Xun's, the methods differed yet both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh Jiang's path and Xun's: different arts, the same fall.

sentences.zh: 以古道而居今世，難乎免矣。

translations.literal: To live by the ancient way in the present age—how could one escape ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Live by the ancient way in the present age—who escapes the end they met?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：謐口禍門，荀言亟盡。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Mi's mouth was the gate of disaster; Xun's words were soon spent.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Mi's mouth opened the gate of ruin; Xun's counsel ran out too soon.

sentences.zh: 時清主異，幷合同殞。

translations.literal: The times were calm yet the lords differed; together they fell and died.
translations.idiomatic: Times were orderly, yet master and man pulled apart—and both went down as one.
